verdict.rationale: Orama's own JavaScript API lets a coding agent work end to end in code: create a database with an indexing schema, add documents with insert/insertMultiple, and run full-text, vector, or hybrid searches, with no dashboard involved. Orama Cloud also offers SDKs and an auto-configured MCP server, but its MCP is documented only for interacting with data, and the server URL is copied manually. missing for 10: evidence that Cloud projects, data sources, and indexes can be created via API, CLI, or MCP rather than the dashboard; a published OpenAPI spec (probe 404s); independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven end-to-end use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can create an index, add documents, and run queries end to end — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching a dashboard

citations.quote: We can create a new instance (from now on database) with an indexing schema. The schema represents the searchable properties of the document to be inserted.
If you have a lot of records, we suggest using the `insertMultiple` function
Hybrid search is an Orama feature that allows you to perform full-text and vector search in one unique query, combining the results to get the best of both worlds.
Every Orama Cloud project comes with an MCP server that is automatically configured to interact with your project's data.
